title: Redwood PLG Quickstart - Discovery with Omnivore Health
next_steps: Send PLG quickstart guide + free credits instructions
Schedule 1:1 SE-led demo and benchmark call next week
action_items: Alex: Email quickstart guide and credit redemption steps (due 2026-04-01)
Priya: Prepare simple latency/cost estimate for Omnivore's 50 rps baseline (due 2026-04-03)
Ellen: Confirm internal stakeholders and pilot success criteria (due 2026-04-02)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 14:00 PDT - 42 mins
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Ellen Park (CTO, Omnivore), Marco Ruiz (ML Eng), Dana Lee (Product), Chris (Procurement)

00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:04 Ellen: yep loud and clear, thanks Alex.
00:07 Alex: cool quick agenda: PLG quickstart and free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private options, and any security questions. then we'll wrap with next steps. sound good?
00:15 Marco: yep that's perfect.
00:18 Priya: just a note I'll jump in with a little architecture sketch when we talk about time-to-first-token.
00:22 Alex: awesome. Ellen can you give us a quick overview of your use case and constraints so we tailor things?
00:30 Ellen: yeah quick context, we are building an LLM assist in the clinical notes workflow. latency matters for in-line suggestions, we also have strict PHI rules, need to know data residency options and KMS support. team is small - Marco is building a prototype. timeline is pilot in 4-6 weeks. budget: prefer to start hosted then consider dedicated or private for production if needed.
00:52 Alex: that's helpful. when you say latency in-line what are you targeting? p95 or p99?
00:57 Marco: p95 under 300ms ideally for short suggestions (~50-100 tokens). throughput currently light but expected spikes during clinician shifts maybe up to 50 rps.
01:10 Priya: ok interesting, that lines up with common PLG->pilot paths. Hosted can often meet that with smaller models and batching, dedicated gives more headroom and private/VPC is what customers choose when PHI policies require. 
01:22 Dana: curious on time-to-first-token - Marco will need to get something running this week, how fast can we go from signup to tokens?
01:29 Alex: with our quickstart you can sign up, redeem free credits, and call the API in under an hour. typical dev flow: signup, API key in console, run the quickstart curl or python snippet, that's your first token. we also have SDKs.
01:40 Marco: are the free credits auto-applied? any form requirements?
01:43 Alex: it's straightforward - we give a free credits promo to new accounts, you'll just need to confirm email and org. for enterprise we can fast-track. I'll include exact steps in the email.
01:51 Ellen: and demo data - can we keep everything in our VPC if we try hosted? we can't send PHI outside.
01:58 Priya: hosted means data goes to Redwood's managed service; we have options - some customers pseudonymize before sending, others run an on-prem/private deployment for PHI. For many pilots teams start hosted with de-identified data, then move to Dedicated or Private for PHI.
02:10 Marco: is there an easy migration path from hosted to dedicated? we don't want big rework.
02:14 Alex: yes it's designed to be smooth - same API surface, same model catalog, you can pin model versions. moving to Dedicated is mostly an infra config and capacity reservation. Priya can explain specifics.
02:24 Priya: from a technical side, the SDK and API calls are identical; the differences are routing and tenancy. For private deployments you manage VPC peering and keys. KV cache behaviors and batching remain consistent. We help with a migration plan and a rollback policy.
02:38 Dana: what about quantization and model options? we might want cheaper smaller models for in-line suggestions.
02:44 Priya: yep we have curated model variants and recommendations; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching settings given your token distribution. For quickstart you'll likely test a smaller open model or gpt-3.5-like variant.
02:58 Marco: any limits on streaming or function calls in quickstart?
03:01 Alex: streaming is enabled, function-style tool calling is available on supported models. quickstart samples include streaming and basic function call examples.
03:08 Chris: procurement question - what contracts or paperwork for free credits? or trial?
03:12 Alex: trial is standard T&Cs, nothing heavy. for production Dedicated/Private we move to a contract. I'll attach our trial terms.
03:19 Ellen: on security we need SOC2 and KMS/HSM details, and audit log examples.
03:24 Priya: we keep an SOC2 pack and a security whitepaper. hosted supports customer-managed KMS integration for key wrapping in some enterprise tiers; for Private you manage keys entirely. audit logs and per-request tracing are in the Console. I'll share the security docs link.
03:35 Marco: performance question - you mentioned 300ms p95 for 50-100 tokens, is that realistic on hosted?
03:40 Priya: it depends on model choice and region; with small model variants and proper batching you can get ~150-300ms p95. If you need consistent <200ms p95 under load, Dedicated with reserved GPUs is safer. We'll provide baseline numbers for your expected workload.
03:54 Alex: I'll add an initial estimate in the follow-up.
03:56 Ellen: great. another point: data residency - we need EU region only for some clients, is that supported for hosted?
04:03 Alex: yes we have regional endpoints; for strict residency on hosted we'll ensure requests are processed in the chosen region. Private is obviously fully controlled.
04:12 Dana: could you walk quick through a demo flow - Marco wants to try calling in code.
04:16 Priya: sure i can outline steps, i'll keep it high level: 1) sign up at console.redwood.ai, 2) create org/project, 3) get API key, 4) run the python quickstart script which hits the /v1/generate endpoint using the small model, 5) inspect tokens and logs in the Console. Typical time-to-first-token is 10-30 minutes if you have credentials handy, under an hour for new org verifies.
04:39 Marco: do you have a sample we can paste?
04:41 Priya: yes, i'll include a python and curl snippet in the follow-up email. it includes streaming example and how to enable function outputs.
04:50 Chris: billing - is there a free tier or just credits? we need to know cost for spikes.
04:55 Alex: free credits only on signup, then pay-as-you-go. we also offer reserved capacity for Dedicated with predictable monthly commit; Optimize helps model selection to reduce per-token cost. I'll include a rough cost worksheet.
05:07 Ellen: what about throttling and quotas? we need to ensure clinician workflows don't get rate-limited in production.
05:12 Priya: quotas and rate limits are configurable per-org and per-api-key; for production you can set a dedicated pool and guaranteed throughput. We can set up alerting via the Console.
05:22 Marco: curious about observability - traces, per-route latency breakdowns?
05:25 Priya: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, latency histograms, per-model dashboards, and traces for request flows. We also support exporting logs to your S3 or SIEM.
05:36 Ellen: any known pitfalls during PLG quickstarts?
05:39 Alex: common ones: sending PHI raw to hosted before legal signoff, not pinning model versions so evals change under you, and ignoring prefix caching which can save costs. We'll call those out in the quickstart doc.
05:51 Marco: ok makes sense. if we sign up today can we get the credits fast?
05:54 Alex: yes typically same day; I'll initiate the promo.
05:56 Dana: what's the next step timeline?
06:00 Alex: recap: I'll email quickstart guide + promo steps + security pack today. Priya will prepare a small latency/cost estimate for your 50 rps baseline and a simple migration checklist to Dedicated/Private. We'll schedule an SE-led demo and benchmark next week.
06:15 Ellen: sounds good thanks everyone.
06:18 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up.
06:20 Jamal: one last note - I'll be your CSM on record, ping me if you need pilot onboarding help.
06:25 Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains minor ASR errors and occasional speaker mislabels. References: shared links to quickstart, security pack, and cost worksheet will be sent.
